decisive_items: High-sensitivity troponin T: 888 ng/L (normal range, 0–14 ng/L)
left anterior descending artery showed a large filling defect in the proximal segment with TIMI flow grade 3
response.rationale: Acute presentation with elevated troponin and a large LAD filling defect with TIMI 3 flow suggests a recanalized thrombotic occlusion, fitting acute MI with recanalization. R10C is broader acute MI but lacks recanalization specificity.

rejected.why: No support; prior MI contradicts vasospasm as primary.
Cardiomyopathy not supported by normal echo and no heart failure.
Thrombosis is too generic; recanalization and MI context more specific.
MINOCA requires non-obstructive coronaries; here LAD has filling defect.
Takotsubo requires wall motion abnormalities, absent.
Bradycardia alone not diagnostic; no arrhythmia evidence.
PE unlikely with normal saturation and no RV strain; troponin pattern more cardiac.
Coronary artery disease is broad and not the acute diagnosis.
SCAD not supported; OCT no dissection evidence.
ACS is umbrella term; less specific than recanalized MI.
